decisions.reason: It builds directly on the firm's core second-channel and encryption capabilities, so its strong in-house R&D and related knowledge make continued improvement and retention likely.
A mobile PDF digital signature function is close to the firm's established authentication and signing know-how, which gives management good absorptive capacity to learn from early use and refine it.
This multi-layer end-to-end security architecture sits squarely within the firm's deepest technical competences and is therefore very likely to be kept as a strategic core offering.

Secure email-to-app delivery matches the firm's move toward secure cross-channel communication, and because it builds on existing capabilities the firm is likely to keep developing rather than abandon it.

The QR-code-based hardware signature token is still close to the firm's offer and supported by existing hardware and security experience, but hardware adoption risk makes it somewhat more droppable than the others.

A payment network security compliance suite builds on the firm's established security and regulatory strengths, so management would likely retain it in a growing market and improve it through internal R&D.
